items.title: 16.2.8 Other Endocrine Glands/Tissues (printed '16.2.8.' with trailing dot)

source_refs.note: Topic 16.2.8, printed as '16.2.8.' (PDF 68-69); Figure 16.6 is replaced by the original diagram.

blocks.text: There are several other endocrine glands, and specialised endocrine cells in the brain, stomach, small intestine, liver and other organs.

blocks.caption: Other endocrine glands and tissues
rows: thymus, beneath the sternum between the lungs
maturation of T cells, which defend the body from pathogens
pineal gland, near the base of the brain
makes the gastric glands release gastric juice
secretin: pancreas releases pancreatic juice; cholecystokinin: gallbladder releases bile
renin controls aldosterone production; erythropoietin makes the bone marrow produce red blood cells; calcitriol raises blood calcium by absorption from the intestine
bind to pain receptors and block the sensation of pain
powerful local vasodilators; involved in inflammation

blocks.alt: A simple outline of a human body with the endocrine glands marked and labelled: hypothalamus, pituitary and pineal gland in the head; thyroid with four small parathyroid glands behind it in the neck; thymus in the chest; adrenal glands on top of the dashed kidneys; pancreas across the abdomen; ovaries in the pelvis of females; and testes outside the abdomen in males.
blocks.caption: Locations of the thymus and pineal glands (original diagram after Figure 16.6).
blocks.long_description: The hypothalamus, pituitary and pineal gland lie in the brain. The thyroid wraps the front of the trachea in the neck, with the parathyroids on its back surface. The thymus lies beneath the sternum between the lungs. An adrenal gland sits on top of each kidney. The pancreas lies in the abdomen. The gonads are the ovaries in females and the testes in males.
